email.body1:
Catie, saw FloQast partner with PwC on close automation and keep scaling past the $100M Series E.

Growth like that usually means more accounts in play than the team can cover before reps ramp, and that is where deals go cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for FloQast off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Catie, quick follow-up for FloQast.

At this scale, the pipeline target moves faster than headcount can. Most inside-sales leaders don't actually know how many meetings the team needs to book to hit the number, so the gap shows up late and the quarter becomes a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings FloQast needs to close that gap this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Catie, last bit of proof for FloQast.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how FloQast's reply rate likely compares to other late-stage SaaS teams. Want to hop on a quick call and I'll walk you through it?
email.body4:
Catie, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Scaling an inside-sales team is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your inside-sales motion? I'll tailor it to FloQast either way.
